holidays.name: International Axe Throwing Day
holidays.description: A day for hurling sharp hatchets at wooden targets, now a legit urban pastime. Lumberjack flannel is optional but strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: Axe throwing grew from lumberjack competitions and took off as a bar-and-venue pastime in Toronto in the late 2000s. The day was created by fans and venues to celebrate the sport's rise.
holidays.funFact: The first indoor axe throwing league was reportedly founded in Toronto in 2011, and the World Axe Throwing League now runs international championships.

holidays.name: Kitten Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the tiniest, fluffiest tornadoes of chaos known to humankind. Cuddle one, adopt one, or just look at pictures of them.
holidays.origin: An unofficial internet-era observance created by animal lovers, often tied to shelters promoting kitten adoption and fostering during peak kitten season in early summer.
holidays.funFact: Kitten season peaks in spring and summer, when shelters can receive hundreds of newborn cats in a single week.

holidays.name: Sewing Machine Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble machine that stitched together the modern world, from blue jeans to superhero capes.
holidays.origin: Commemorates the birthday of Elias Howe, whose 1846 patent for a lockstitch sewing machine revolutionized the clothing industry. Sewing enthusiasts and crafters mark the day.
holidays.funFact: Howe reportedly got the idea for the needle placement from a dream in which he was captured by cannibals whose spears had holes near the tips.

holidays.name: Random Acts of Kindness Day (Unofficial Observance)
holidays.description: A day for tossing out spontaneous good deeds, like paying for a stranger's coffee or leaving encouraging sticky notes in public places.
holidays.origin: Part of the wider kindness movement popularized by the Random Acts of Kindness Foundation, with various communities and groups adopting different dates to spread goodwill.
holidays.funFact: Studies on kindness suggest that performing small acts of generosity can boost the giver's happiness as much as it does the recipient's.

holidays.name: Weed Your Garden Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to grabbing your gloves and declaring war on dandelions, crabgrass, and every other uninvited green guest in your flower beds.
holidays.origin: A gardening observance that falls in mid-June when weeds are at their most aggressive, encouraging gardeners to get ahead of the invasion before summer takes over.
holidays.funFact: A single dandelion plant can produce up to 2,000 seeds per year, each able to travel miles on the wind.
